correctness.rationale: At n=6 symmetry gives all three coefficients zero. For n>6, Simmons' theorem gives \(\alpha_1>0\). The exact identity \(\Pr(X=6)/\Pr(X=0)-1=(x-3)Q(x)/(80x^5)\), with \(x=n-3\ge4\) and \(Q(x)=x^4+246x^3+333(x-4)^2+2448(x-4)+4140>0\), gives \(\alpha_3<0\). With only \(\alpha_2\) between them, condition \(L_1\) follows for either sign of \(\alpha_2\). Quantifiers and boundary n=6 are explicit; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Mean three is not an arbitrary numerical slice: the source explicitly proves means one and two, then a different range beginning at mean four, making m=3 the isolated first missing integer-mean case of its stated binomial analysis. Settling all n>=6 closes that natural gap and immediately makes the source's convolution tail theorem available whenever the added binomial summand has mean three. The proof identifies a reusable endpoint mechanism rather than a finite computation.
